pages.text: The $(thing)Tobacco Drying Rack$() turns raw leaf into cured leaf. A rack holds up to $(item)16$() identical raw leaves. Leaves in one rack must be the same item with the same components/quality data. Looking at the rack shows its live $(item)X/16 Leaves$() count.

pages.title: Tobacco Drying Rack
pages.text: Craft the rack before choosing a curing environment.

Right-click the rack with raw tobacco to add one leaf. Empty-hand right-click removes the batch. Sneak-right-click reports detailed status. The visible rack progresses through empty, low, medium, and full load models. Once curing reaches $(item)10%$(), the batch locks and no more leaves may be added until it is removed or finished.
pages.title: Loading the Rack

pages.text: The rack automatically chooses the strongest valid method each tick in this order: $(thing)Fire → Flue → Sun → Air$(). You do not select a mode in a menu; the structure and environment select it for you. With Create installed, fan airflow reaching either the lower or upper section can assist a valid cure.
pages.title: Automatic Method
Industrial Drying Rack
pages.text: With $(thing)Create$() installed, the $(item)Industrial Drying Rack$() is a 32-leaf automation-only factory rack. It has no internal fan or power connector: external Create airflow is required for all curing. Assisted Air/Sun and Fire/Flue curing is modestly faster than the wooden rack, with identical quality rules.

pages.title: Traditional Alternative
pages.text: A Drying Rack is not required. Sneak-right-click the underside of a sturdy block while holding 16 matching raw or cured leaves to make a traditional hanging bunch. In Creative mode, one held leaf is enough to place the 16-leaf bunch. Raw bunches cure by the same methods; cured bunches can be hung for decoration/storage but expose no inventory automation or Display Link.

Vanilla hoppers can automate racks. Insert raw leaves from a horizontal side; top and bottom cannot insert. A hopper underneath can extract only after curing is complete. Create/NeoForge capability automation still respects the rack’s validation and finished-output rules.
